title: SWCraft needs mapping
description: How a requirements team's Sphinx-Needs needs map to SWCraft's requirements, passed to `swcraft import requirements --mapping FILE`. It maps the team's need types and field names to SWCraft's; a key left out keeps SWCraft's own name. It is never a key of `swcraft.yaml`, and it lies outside the model root.

types.description: The team's need type (the directive name, the need's `type`) mapped to `req`, `spec` or `ignore`. A need of an `ignore` type is not imported. When present, this is the whole list: a type it does not name is refused. When absent, `req` and `spec` map to themselves.

fields.description: Per SWCraft field, the key of the team's need it is read from. A field left out keeps its default source. The id and the type are never mapped.

removed_status.description: The statuses that remove a requirement from the model, each listed once. When absent, `rejected` alone.

ignore.description: The team's own need keys SWCraft does not hold, each listed once. Listing a link type ignores its `_back` mirror with it. Any other key SWCraft does not read is refused.

FieldSources.description: Per SWCraft field, the key of the team's need it is read from.

title.description: The need key the requirement's `title` is read from.

description.description: The need key the requirement's `description` is read from: Sphinx-Needs writes the directive body as `content`, taken as written.

asil.description: The need key the requirement's `asil` is read from.

document.description: The need key the requirement's `document` is read from.

revision.description: The need key the requirement's `revision` (the source tool's own revision) is read from.

derived_from.description: The need key the requirement's parents are read from. A link field's part and condition are dropped, so `REQ-1.p1[status=="open"]` names `REQ-1`.

status.description: The need key the status is read from. It is not stored; it decides removal (`removed_status`).
